slides.title: 5 phrases no textbook will teach you
slides.sub: Your textbook lied to you. Politely.

slides.meaning: “I wish!” — the official reply to every dream that will never come true.
“No idea.” A complete sentence. Some say a philosophy.
slides.ex_en: “When does the train arrive?” “Only God knows.”

slides.meaning: Means “come on”, “hurry up”, “no way” and “please”. Good luck.
“Thank goodness.” Mostly used in food-related emergencies.
“How cool!” Very informal. Never say it to your boss. Or to a nonna.
slides.ex_it: «Il capo ci dà il venerdì libero!» «Che figata!»

slides.title: Which one will you use first?
slides.text: Comment your favourite. Your Italian teacher doesn't need to know.

caption:
5 Italian phrases no textbook will teach you 🇮🇹

Magari · Boh · Dai · Meno male · Che figata

Your textbook taught you “Dov'è la biblioteca?”. Italians taught us these. Guess which ones you'll actually use.

Save this before your next trip — and tell us your favourite 👇

🇮🇹 Italiani: quale manca? Sappiamo che ne avete almeno altre cento.
